Complete one row at a time for your proposal. Write each answer as the sentence you would put in the paper. This checklist follows the [data checklist](data-checklist.qmd) from Lecture 5.5. Rows marked **[6.x]** are covered in that lecture. Sources: **B** = Bellemare, "How to Write Applied Papers in Economics," Section 5; **AJAE** = AJAE Author Guidelines and Author's Final Checklist. Unmarked rows are course standards.

## Estimation strategy

| # | The section states | Your answer |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Prediction to equation [6.1].** Which testable prediction from your conceptual framework (Unit 4) each equation tests. | |
| 2 | **Estimating equation [6.1, B].** The equation, with every variable and coefficient defined, subscripts ordered from smallest to largest unit, and a separate coefficient label for each specification. | |
| 3 | **Unit of observation [6.1].** What one row is. It matches the observation unit and key in your data section (Unit 5). | |
| 4 | **Parameter of interest [6.1].** Which coefficient answers the question, its units, how to read a one-unit change, and whether it has a causal interpretation (if not, what it describes). | |
| 5 | **Estimator [6.1, B].** The estimation method (for example, OLS, linear probability model, probit, maximum likelihood, GMM) and why. | |
| 6 | **Inference [6.1, B].** The null hypothesis; what the standard errors are robust to; the clustering level and why; how few clusters are handled; whether sampling weights are used. | |

## Identification strategy

| # | The section states | Your answer |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | **Identifying assumption [6.1].** The assumption in one plain sentence, with no notation. | |
| 8 | **Identifying variation [6.1].** Which comparison (across units, over time, at a threshold, from assignment) moves the treatment and not the outcome directly. | |
| 9 | **Threats [6.1, B].** Whether each applies, and how the paper handles it in the design or a robustness check: reverse causality; unobserved heterogeneity; measurement error; spillovers across units or periods. | |

## Additional rows by design

| # | If the paper... | The section states | Your answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | Estimates a structural model **[6.2]** | The primitives; which variation identifies which parameter; the estimator in one paragraph, details in an appendix; fit or validation; the counterfactuals the model is used for. | |
| 11 | Uses a prediction step **[6.3]** | Which step is prediction and which is a causal parameter; how the predictor is tuned and evaluated; how the prediction error affects the parameter of interest. | |
| 12 | Collects primary data or runs an experiment **[6.4, AJAE]** | Assignment or sampling; sample size and why it is enough; IRB approval; the instrument or instructions in an appendix that does not identify the authors. | |
| 13 | Uses qualitative or mixed methods **[6.4]** | How cases or participants are selected; how evidence is coded; what question the qualitative evidence answers that the quantitative evidence cannot. | |

## Scope and placement

| # | The section states | Your answer |
|---|---|---|
| 14 | **What the design does not identify [6.5].** Parameters, mechanisms, or populations outside the estimand; limits on external validity. | |
| 15 | **Robustness and sensitivity [6.5, B].** Three checks a referee would request, each tied to a threat in row 9 or to the inference choices in row 6. | |
| 16 | **Appendix [AJAE].** Which implementation details move to the appendix, cited in the text as an online appendix, not "available on request." | |
| 17 | **Replication [AJAE].** The data, code or pseudo-code, and README to be shared, or the confidentiality restriction to raise with the editor at submission. | |
